pr.title: Plan handing a finished spec to the user for review
pr.head: 984cbf97a65c80846318fc175159fd835ec368b2

summary: Projector's spec skill writes a project's plan under docs/projects/. Today it ends by leaving the plan uncommitted, and it opens a pull request only when someone asks for one. When it does open one, it marks the pull request ready right away, and the only hand-off is a URL in the conversation.

This pull request adds a plan, spec-handover, at status: ready. The plan has spec commit the plan on a branch, open a draft pull request, and post one inbox request that links to the plan as GitHub renders it. The pull request stays a draft until the user answers. Looks good or a decline marks it ready with project review ready, and Some feedback makes spec revise the plan and reopen the same request.

The draft hold makes the user's review come before the automated one. A session that reviews the whole repository skips drafts, so the automated review starts only once the user has read the plan. The pull request changes no code. It records the design and lists the files a later pull request will change.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Inbox: Projector's panel above the user's prompt, where a session posts an ask (a decision), a tell (news), or a request (work only the user can do).
  • Draft hold: keeping a pull request a draft while a request waits on the user. implement already does this for a device test.
  • Generated section: the Projector block in AGENTS.md that project init writes from src/projector/templates/agents-block.md.

cards.title: Where the review stands
cards.html:
• The first review requested changes with two findings. The plan left two skills that would still mark a waiting plan pull request ready, and it listed a whitespace check that could not fail.
  • Three later commits fixed both and named exactly what the skills/spec/SKILL.md change replaces. The second review is clean.
  • The plan's one open question, a session that ends without cleanup, is deferred on purpose and blocks nothing.
  • project check passes, and the branch merges into the current main without a conflict.

groups.title: The spec-handover plan
groups.kicker: How spec opens a draft pull request and asks the user to review the plan
intro: The plan is the whole pull request. Section 2.1 gives the steps spec takes once the plan passes project check. Section 2.2 gives the fields of the inbox request. Section 2.3 lists the files the implementation changes. Section 3 explains the design, including why the user's review comes first.

Read it against the skills it changes. spec's "Validate and hand over" section is what the plan replaces. implement's "Hand the work over" section has the draft hold the plan reuses, and cleanup lists a held draft as unfinished work. The plan also widens the same draft rule in fix-pr and in work, the skill that keeps a session working while the user is away.

files.note: The new plan: the hand-over flow, the review request, the files it changes, and the acceptance criteria.

checks.text: The plan's claims about the current skills match the head: spec leaves the plan uncommitted, implement keeps a draft while a test request waits and marks it ready on Looks good or a decline, and cleanup marks a held draft ready when the user leaves it. Checked by reading each skill at the head.

Steps 2 and 3 use git diff --check origin/<default-branch>...HEAD. A temporary repository showed that the bare form misses both an untracked plan file and a committed one, and that the range form reports both.

The fix-pr and work rows quote the sentences those skills carry on main exactly. Both sentences keep a draft only for a test request, so each needs the plan review request added. skills/work/SKILL.md is on main but not at this branch's base, so the implementation starts from current main.
